text: Runaway Tram is a steel family roller coaster located at Morey's Piers' Surfside Pier in North Wildwood, New Jersey. It replaced the aging Flitzer roller coaster, which had opened in 1983 and was manufactured in 1969, and required the reconfiguration of seven existing attractions, including the Doo Wopper, at a total investment of $4 million. The Flitzer was retired in September 2018 after evaluations determined it was too old to operate safely despite numerous refurbishments, with its final day of operation on September 30, 2018. Preparation began in October 2018 when the Flitzer, Doo Wopper, and other attractions were dismantled, and the dormant Formula One Raceway, which had closed in 2016 and was located underneath the pier, was also gutted. On January 10, 2019, Morey's Piers officially announced Runaway Tram as the Flitzer's replacement, set to debut in time for the park's 50th anniversary. Part of the pier was removed and footers were poured into the ground below in April 2019, on space formerly occupied by the Raceway. Vertical construction began shortly after, and the coaster train arrived on May 8, 2019. Testing started on June 17, 2019, with an original opening date of July 2, 2019, for the 4th of July long weekend, but an unprecedentedly slow approval process delayed the opening. Runaway Tram opened to the public on August 9, 2019, after state approval. The coaster is 36 feet (11 m) tall, 922 feet (281 m) long, and reaches speeds of up to 28.6 mph (46.0 km/h). It features a single 10-car train with 2 riders per car, totaling 20 riders, and occupies a 194.6' x 87.9' site, supported by 118 columns. Manufactured by Zierer as a Force 281 variant, which includes a single booster wheel lift hill and helix along with various twists and turns, Runaway Tram is one of only four such models built, including Flight School (2019) at Emerald Park in Ireland and Flyvende Ørn (2018) at Legoland Billund Resort in Denmark. The latter coaster influenced Runaway Tram's design, as Morey's representatives had ridden it during a 2018 Scandinavia business trip and found it suitable for the park. The ride's train and station are modeled after the local Wildwood Sightseer Tramcar, a trackless train service originally built for the 1939 New York World's Fair and debuting on the Wildwood Boardwalk in June 1949. The themed train and station were designed by Cincinnati-based firm JRA, and the custom LED signage was designed and manufactured by local firm A.B.S. Sign Company.
